simple.meaning: דָּחַק (dâchaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to press , i.e. oppress.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Judges, Joel, beginning at Judges 2:18. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּחַק (H1766) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: דָּחַק (dâchaq) / H1766 is traced through Judges 2:18, Joel 2:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: When Yahweh raised up judges for them, then Yahweh was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for it grieved Yahweh because of their groaning by reason of those who oppressed them and troubled them.
